mechanism: When recent volatility is low, aggregate load follows a stable daily calendar shape, so same-hour historical segments are more predictive than volatile periods.
When recent volatility is high, volatility tends to cluster, so historical segments with similarly high volatility and large recent differences are more informative.
When recent slope magnitude is high, the series is in a ramp phase, and the shape of similar ramps at the same hour is more predictive.
On workdays, aggregate load has a strong industrial/commercial component and a stable diurnal pattern, so workday history is more predictive than weekend history.
On weekends, aggregate load lacks much of the workday industrial/commercial demand, so weekend history is more predictive and workday history can be misleading.
In summer and winter, seasonal heating/cooling demand creates distinct load level and shape regimes, so same-season historical segments are more predictive.
When recent autocorrelation is low, the recent trajectory is noisy and less informative, so calendar structure should dominate retrieval.
When load is high and recent autocorrelation is high, the series is in a persistent peak plateau, so similar high-level persistent segments are more informative.
When recent volatility is high, volatility regimes repeat across calendar seasons, so cross-season historical analogs with similar volatility transfer more reliably than same-season segments.
Morning ramps are dominated by a consistent start-of-day load pickup, so high recent slope in the morning is best matched to same-hour historical segments across both workdays and weekends.
Non-working days have a distinct lower and later-starting load profile from workdays, so restricting to non_working history matches that structure.

When recent autocorrelation is low, the recent trajectory is noisy but the current level and volatility still carry information about the near-future distribution, so matching those summary statistics is safer than matching the noisy trajectory.

Persistent high-load plateaus are primarily shaped by the workday/non-working-day demand structure, so high and persistent load should retrieve historical workday analogs with similar level rather than forcing the same hour.
